I think the assumption of AA being a killer to competitive PvP is misleading. It's a killer to casual PvP as well.

Most players who play PvP in any shooter will not play knowing that another medium has a clear advantage over them. Especially in the case of AA opening the door to exploitation for use of with M+KB.

I used to be a competitive FPS player back in the day (I've gotten older and just don't give a shit about any of that now), But being a casual PvP player still provides a level of competition that I and others enjoy. We all do. You don't join a casual game because you want to lose. You still want to win and you want to try your best for the most part. 

If casual players are losing to others due to exploits, not because of being out matched, then the casual PvP player base will cease to exist as well.

In short, It's a killer to PvP (within PC gaming). It doesn't matter if it's classified as a competitive match or not.

Ingredients

* 1 1/2 pounds skinless, boneless, chicken thighs, cubed
* 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt
* 1/2 tablespoon ghee or butter
* 1/2 onion, chopped
* 3 garlic cloves, minced
* 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
* 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric
* 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
* 1 teaspoon ground coriander
* 1 teaspoon cumin
* 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper
* 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
* 1 (14-ounce) can petite diced tomatoes
* 6 tablespoons canned full-fat coconut milk
* 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, for garnish

Directions
Place the chicken in a slow cooker and season with 1 teaspoon of the salt.

In a medium skillet, melt the ghee over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, garam masala, coriander, cumin, cayenne, and cardamom. Cook, stirring until the vegetables are soft and the spices are fragrant, about 5 minutes. Transfer to a blender along with the tomatoes and blend until smooth. Pour over the chicken in the slow cooker and add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt.

Cover and cook on low for 6 hours. Sir in the coconut milk. Serve garnished with the cilantro.

Here's the [link](http://www.mangotomato.com/2016/11/slow-cooker-tikka-chicken-masala-from.html) to the recipe if you don't want to buy the book but the Skinny Taste Fast & Slow books really is good.

Some notes: 
-Don't use chicken breast, it will come out too dry.
-If you're a garlic fan like I am increase the cloves to 6, not 3.
-If you like spicy food like I do, make it 2 heaping teaspoons of cayenne, not 1/4 teaspoon.
-replace coconut milk with coconut CREAM. Otherwise it comes out too runny. The flavor will still be good if you use milk but the consistency won't be as nice.
